introduction_section.heading: What is
content: Security testing is the rigorous process of evaluating your software to uncover vulnerabilities, threats, and risks. Instead of waiting for a malicious attack to reveal the weak points in your system, our certified ethical hackers take the offensive, attempting to breach your applications using the exact same tools and techniques as real-world cybercriminals.

At Devisgon, we go beyond automated scans. We dive deep into your application's logic, APIs, and infrastructure to find hidden loopholes like SQL injections, cross-site scripting (XSS), and broken authentication. We then provide actionable remediation steps to lock down your system completely.
introduction_section.highlight_quote: “If you think compliance is expensive, try a data breach.”

case_study_section.headline: Prevented a massive data leak in a healthcare portal

problem.label: Problem
problem.text: A telehealth startup was weeks away from launching their patient portal but needed a final security audit to comply with HIPAA regulations.

solution.label: Solution
solution.text: During our manual penetration test, we discovered a severe Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) vulnerability that allowed any user to access other patients' medical records by manipulating the URL.

faq_section.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq_section.subtitle: Get answers about cybersecurity and penetration testing

questions.question: What is the difference between a Vulnerability Scan and a Penetration Test?
questions.answer: A Vulnerability Scan is an automated process that checks your systems for known flaws and reports them. A Penetration Test (Pentest) is a manual, human-led process where an ethical hacker actively tries to exploit those flaws to see how deep into the system they can get, simulating a real-world attack.

questions.question: Is it safe to perform security testing on a live, production environment?
questions.answer: While we can test production environments carefully, we highly recommend performing intrusive security testing (like Penetration Testing) on a staging or replica environment. This ensures there is absolutely no disruption to your live users or risk of accidental data corruption.

questions.question: How often should we perform security testing?
questions.answer: Best practices dictate running automated vulnerability scans continuously (integrated into your CI/CD pipeline). Deep-dive manual penetration tests should be conducted at least annually, or immediately following any major architecture change or significant feature release.

questions.question: What happens after you find a vulnerability?
questions.answer: We don't just hand you a list of problems. We provide a detailed report ranking the vulnerabilities by severity (Critical, High, Medium, Low) alongside step-by-step remediation instructions. Once your developers apply the fix, we perform a 're-test' to guarantee the loophole is permanently closed.
